The unchanged baseline top8 contains zero direct declared-biographical-background matches; the South Korea fragment is only rank 87 in top128. Five additions supply distinct missing relations, not fixed-place aliases.

confusion_boundaries.criterion: A biographical place attaches to a person; a visible backdrop attaches to the scene. Neither relation entails the other.

confusion_boundaries.distinction: Upbringing versus birthplace, citizenship, ancestry or residence
confusion_boundaries.criterion: Retain only the type of relation actually supplied. A hometown claim does not fill all national or life-history fields.
A supplied statement remains attributed; the research sources do not certify any individual history.
No facial feature, skin color, hairstyle, clothing, expression, dialect stereotype or personality label verifies a hometown or nationality.
Contextual attribution does not authorize a caption inside the image, signage, identification card, flag or regional landmark.

recommendations: Integrate the five distinct contextual mechanisms only after source/native review; do not multiply city or country aliases.
Retain an actual independent declaration witness with the main subject and source scope. The draft frozen_value guard is deliberately fail-closed pending this witness.
Run the original task-input query unchanged before/after; keep additional intents separate, and assess all top8 meanings rather than CID presence alone.
Do not add appearance cues or mandatory props to make a nonvisual biographical claim look observable. Rendered pixels can be reviewed for unwanted stereotypes or text, but cannot prove the claim.

research_sources.title: IPTC Photo Metadata User Guide
research_sources.supports: Person metadata is separately represented from image pixels; Location Created and Location Shown describe two photographic location concepts, not the subject's biography.

research_sources.title: US Census Bureau: Place of Birth, Citizenship, Year of Entry
research_sources.supports: Place of birth, citizenship and entry history are collected as separate questions. A birthplace does not supply citizenship or a life chronology.

research_sources.title: US Census Bureau: About Ancestry
research_sources.supports: Ancestry concerns ethnic origin, descent or heritage and is conceptually different from the photographic scene location.

research_sources.title: AABA Statement on Race and Racism
research_sources.supports: Human biological variation, including facial features, skin and hair, does not map into discrete racial types. This supports rejecting appearance-based background stereotypes; it does not validate any individual biographical claim.

authored_scene_status: All proposed portrait applications are authored illustrations of source-supported distinctions. They are not quoted source examples, source endorsement, individual biography verification, or native approval.

additional_test_intents.role_focus: Keep the stated childhood home and current residence as distinct stages belonging to the same adult, preserving their supplied sequence.
additional_test_intents.scene_context: An adult now living in Lisbon describes an earlier childhood in Recife; the studio has no geographic scenery.

additional_test_intents.role_focus: Retain a supplied birth city with birthplace scope while citizenship and ancestry remain unspecified.
additional_test_intents.scene_context: An adult portrait brief identifies only the subject's birthplace and uses a plain indoor setting.

additional_test_intents.role_focus: Attribute the origin statement to the supplied biography while keeping photographic location separate.
additional_test_intents.scene_context: An adult is photographed in a rented Berlin studio; an accompanying biography names a different place of origin.
